A Norway maple, marked invasive in Vermont, 4 m from a native sugar maple (UVM-4181). Snap a leaf stalk: Norway maple's sap is milky, sugar maple's clear.
A Scotch pine, 29 m from a native eastern white pine (UVM-0588). Count the needles in a bundle: two, short and twisted, against white pine's five, long and soft.
A Norway spruce, 6 m from a native white spruce (UVM-4005). Norway spruce's side branches hang like curtains and its cones are long; white spruce's cones are short.
A Lombardy poplar, 5 m from a native bigtooth aspen (UVM-4011): a narrow column grown from cuttings of one male tree, beside an aspen with big, coarse teeth on its leaves.
A young kousa dogwood, 16 m from a young native flowering dogwood (UVM-4726). Kousa blooms weeks later, with pointed bracts; flowering dogwood's bracts are notched.
A Colorado blue spruce, from the Rockies, 5 m from a native white spruce (UVM-4185): stiff, sharp, blue-gray needles against white spruce's softer green.
